channel.title: The New Yorker — Reporting
channel.description: Latest reporting from The New Yorker

item.title: When A.I. Is a Member of the Family
item.description: A single mom, her two daughters, and the chatbots that fill in the gaps.

item.title: Rope-a-Dope
item.description: Are the Enhanced Games an existential threat to fairness or a cure for death?

item.title: How Biden Enabled Israel’s Aggression Toward Gaza—and Iran
item.description: Top officials from the previous Administration now express regret over their failure to rein in Netanyahu.

item.title: One Man’s Quest to Fix Every Deadly Guardrail
item.description: In 2016, Steve Eimers’s daughter died when she hit a defective guardrail. Then he learned that the country was full of them.

item.title: María Corina Machado’s Opposition in Exile
item.description: The Venezuelan politician hoped to become her country’s leader with help from the U.S. The Trump Administration had other priorities.

item.title: Florentina Holzinger’s Naked Ambition
item.description: The artist’s extreme use of the body has caused viewers to puke, faint, and leave her shows. At the Venice Biennale, though, her vision has made her a star.

item.title: A Woman Lost Two Partners to Guns—Then the N.R.A. Came to Collect
item.description: The majority of suicides in the U.S. involve guns, and eighty per cent of those are done by white men, a pattern that the gun-rights organization has spent decades denying.

item.title: What Would It Mean to See a New Color?
item.description: Olo can be described as the “greenest green,” though it can never be captured by a camera. But its development tells us a lot about our color vision.

item.title: Johnny Knoxville, America’s God of Mischief
item.description: What moves the star of “Jackass” to risk his life for our entertainment? A very serious investigation.

item.title: How Netanyahu’s Top General Became His Strongest Challenger
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot, whose view of war is shaped by the loss of his son, is, in manner and character, the anti-Bibi.
